title: Estey and Curtis Drug Store before 1907
description: Estey and Curtis Drug Store began in a small shop inside the Taylor Block at King (later Orser) Street and Main Street, Hartland. Samuel Miller founded it in 1895, naming the store after Dr. Isaac Curtis and Dr. Alfred Estey. In 1897, Miller bought the Hartland Drug Store’s inventory and expanded the business to offer a wide range of medicines and sundries at low prices. He later partnered with Frank A. Aiton. The shop quickly outgrew its original space, so on August 2, 1911, Miller bought a larger brick building from John T. G. Carr. (Current headquarters of Day & Ross in 2026)
